evidence_summary: SP-A suppressed TLR-ligand-induced inflammatory mediators through a TLR2-dependent mechanism and reduced inflammation-induced preterm delivery in mice; IL-10 and CXCL1 responses were increased in the protective context.
limitations: The functional paper tests SP-A as a collectin family product in mouse macrophages and pregnancy models, not an SFTPA1-specific recombinant isoform or SCI receiver-cell model. TLR2 dependence is supported, but the complete terminal transcriptional program is not resolved.
consolidation_note: Batch 257 qualified SP-A/TLR2 family-level recovery; SFTPA1 versus SFTPA2 isoform attribution remains unresolved and the evidence is non-exportable.

evidence_summary: BOC and CDON bound Sonic hedgehog specifically in primary biochemical assays; BOC was expressed by commissural neurons and functionally behaved as a Shh receptor in the axon-guidance system.
limitations: The PubMed abstract establishes specific BOC/SHH binding and receptor-dependent axon guidance, but the retrieved packet does not provide a purified affinity constant or native SCI injury model. BOC is a coreceptor/receptor component rather than a standalone canonical GPCR or kinase.
consolidation_note: Batch 258 supervised SHH/BOC recovery; direct, receptor-complex relay, and functional layers remain separate.

evidence_summary: BOC formed a distinct SHH receptor complex with PTCH1 and was required for SHH-dependent signaling; a lipid-dependent coreceptor relay further showed CDON/BOC can bind SCUBE-SHH and hand off SHH through GAS1 to PTCH1 to initiate signaling.
limitations: The receptor-complex studies establish pathway-level relay and coreceptor organization rather than a single BOC-to-TF molecular edge. SHH lipidation, SCUBE binding, receptor stoichiometry, and cell context constrain the relay; no SCI receiver-cell model was tested.
consolidation_note: Batch 258 supervised SHH/BOC recovery; direct, receptor-complex relay, and functional layers remain separate.

evidence_summary: BOC loss or knockdown impaired SHH-mediated commissural-axon attraction, and BOC/CO-RECEPTOR receptor-complex biology supported SHH-dependent cerebellar granule-neuron progenitor proliferation when the complementary coreceptor context was present.
limitations: The functional studies are developmental neural models with receptor-complex redundancy and context dependence. GLI pathway activity is part of Hedgehog signaling, but no direct SHH-to-GLI molecular interaction or universal terminal TF target is inferred.
consolidation_note: Batch 258 supervised SHH/BOC recovery; direct, receptor-complex relay, and functional layers remain separate.

evidence_summary: The Sonic hedgehog N-terminal domain formed a calcium-dependent complex with the third fibronectin type III repeat of mammalian CDO/CDON; biochemical, biophysical, and X-ray structural studies mapped the interface and showed that disease-associated SHH mutations disrupt receptor interaction.
limitations: The structural paper uses recombinant domains and does not model native SCI receiver cells. CDO/CDON is a ligand-binding coreceptor, and the full-length receptor-complex stoichiometry and lipidated SHH presentation are context dependent.
consolidation_note: Batch 259 supervised SHH/CDON recovery; direct, receptor-proximal/pathway, and functional layers remain separate.

evidence_summary: Cdo/CDON positively regulated SHH pathway activity at signal reception and in a parallel mechanism affecting Gli transcriptional activity; Cdo cooperated with GAS1 to promote SHH signaling during neural-tube and craniofacial patterning.
limitations: The studies support pathway position and genetic cooperation but do not identify every immediate adaptor or kinase, and they do not establish a universal GLI terminal target. CDON, GAS1, PTCH1, and BOC remain distinct receptor-complex components.
consolidation_note: Batch 259 supervised SHH/CDON recovery; direct, receptor-proximal/pathway, and functional layers remain separate.

evidence_summary: Cdo/CDON loss reduced SHH-dependent ventral forebrain and floor-plate development and produced holoprosencephaly-like phenotypes; Cdo and Gas1 cooperation supported SHH-dependent neural-tube, craniofacial, and vertebral patterning.
limitations: The output is embryonic developmental patterning with coreceptor redundancy and tissue-specific roles, not an SCI model. No direct CDON-to-GLI binding or terminal target-gene locus is inferred.
consolidation_note: Batch 259 supervised SHH/CDON recovery; direct, receptor-proximal/pathway, and functional layers remain separate.

evidence_summary: Cell-surface binding, in vitro activity, and explant assays identified a specific SHH binding surface for GAS1; the HPE-associated SHH N115K mutation severely reduced SHH/GAS1 binding and signaling activity.
limitations: The study uses cell-surface and recombinant/mutant systems rather than an SCI receiver-cell model. GAS1 is a GPI-linked coreceptor and can act with PTCH1, CDON, BOC, and SCUBE carriers; those complexes are not collapsed into the binary binding edge.
consolidation_note: Batch 260 supervised SHH/GAS1 recovery; direct, receptor-complex relay, and functional layers remain separate.

evidence_summary: GAS1 catalyzed assembly of the signaling-competent SHH/PTCH1 complex by direct transfer of lipidated SHH from the SCUBE2 carrier to PTCH1; structural and structure-guided experiments mapped palmitate/cholesterol recognition and PTCH1 dimerization/internalization.
limitations: This is a receptor-complex and ligand-transfer mechanism, not a standalone intracellular kinase-to-TF map. SHH lipidation, SCUBE2 carrier state, receptor stoichiometry, and engineered-system context constrain the result; no SCI receiver-cell validation was performed.
consolidation_note: Batch 260 supervised SHH/GAS1 recovery; direct, receptor-complex relay, and functional layers remain separate.

source_locator: PMID:17525797; PMCID:PMC1868789; DOI:10.1172/JCI32032; PMID:17504941; PMCID:PMC1865495; DOI:10.1101/gad.1543607; data/raw/evidence/module20_24_supervised_cli_phase2/retry_A20B_SHH_GAS1_selected_records.xml; data/raw/evidence/module20_24_supervised_cli_phase2/retry_A20B_SHH_GAS1_PMC1868789_fulltext.xml; data/raw/evidence/module20_24_supervised_cli_phase2/retry_A20B_SHH_GAS1_PMC1865495_fulltext.xml
evidence_summary: Gas1 loss caused dose-dependent forebrain, facial, skeletal, and neural-tube patterning defects consistent with reduced SHH signaling; Gas1 and Cdo cooperated to promote SHH-dependent neural-tube, craniofacial, and vertebral development.
limitations: The outputs are developmental and tissue-specific, with cooperative/redundant CDON/BOC/PTCH1 context. No direct GAS1-to-GLI molecular interaction or SCI receiver-cell model was established.
consolidation_note: Batch 260 supervised SHH/GAS1 recovery; direct, receptor-complex relay, and functional layers remain separate.

species_support: mouse; chick or rat comparator not established in abstract
evidence_summary: The primary study reports that SHH binds to the heparan-sulfate proteoglycan GPC1 in commissural neurons and uses GPC1 as a coreceptor for SHH-dependent induction of Hhip.
limitations: The accessible primary abstract establishes SHH/GPC1 binding and coreceptor function but does not provide a purified affinity measurement in the retrieved packet. GPC1 is a heparan-sulfate proteoglycan and its presentation/ECM context is important.
consolidation_note: Batch 261 supervised SHH/GPC1 recovery; coreceptor binding, relay, and functional layers remain separate.

evidence_summary: GPC1 was required as a coreceptor for SHH-dependent induction of the Hhip receptor in commissural neurons; the study separates an early transcription-independent SHH attraction response from a later GPC1/Hhip-dependent repulsive response.
limitations: The relay is stage-specific and depends on axon crossing state. It does not establish a universal SHH/GPC1 pathway in all cell types or a direct molecular GPC1-to-TF interaction.
consolidation_note: Batch 261 supervised SHH/GPC1 recovery; coreceptor binding, relay, and functional layers remain separate.

evidence_summary: GPC1-dependent SHH signaling enabled postcrossing commissural axons to respond to a repulsive anteroposterior SHH gradient through Hhip, producing the axon-guidance switch required for normal trajectory selection.
limitations: The output is a developmental commissural-axon model with stage-specific receptor switching. Hhip is an intermediary receptor/antagonist, not a terminal TF, and the result does not define a universal GPC1 function in SCI.
consolidation_note: Batch 261 supervised SHH/GPC1 recovery; coreceptor binding, relay, and functional layers remain separate.

evidence_summary: Comparative recombinant Hedgehog assays report that HHIP/Hip binds SHH, with related Hedgehog ligands showing similar binding responses to Hip and PTCH.
limitations: The retrieved primary abstract supports direct binding in a comparative Hh-binding assay but does not provide a purified affinity constant in the accessible record. HHIP is an extracellular antagonist/modulator, and the exact stoichiometry and tissue-specific contribution remain context-dependent.
consolidation_note: Batch 262 supervised SHH/HHIP recovery; direct binding, extracellular antagonist relay, and functional layers remain separate.

species_support: human; endothelial model and recombinant ligand context
evidence_summary: HHIP attenuated SHH-induced PTCH1 transcription and inhibited Hedgehog-dependent endothelial responses, supporting extracellular sequestration or antagonism upstream of PTCH1 rather than an intracellular kinase relay.
limitations: The evidence supports extracellular antagonism/sequestration and downstream Hedgehog-response attenuation, but does not resolve whether all effects are due to ligand capture versus additional cell-surface mechanisms. It does not establish a universal TF endpoint or SCI-specific transfer.
consolidation_note: Batch 262 supervised SHH/HHIP recovery; direct binding, extracellular antagonist relay, and functional layers remain separate.

evidence_summary: Loss of Hhip increased Hedgehog signaling in the pancreas anlage, impaired pancreas morphogenesis and islet formation, and altered endocrine proliferation; genetic interaction with Ptch1 supported pathway restraint by Hhip.
limitations: This is a mouse developmental model and establishes a functional Hedgehog restraint role, not a universal terminal transcription-factor assignment. It does not establish SCI transfer or a direct HHIP-to-TF interaction.
consolidation_note: Batch 262 supervised SHH/HHIP recovery; direct binding, extracellular antagonist relay, and functional layers remain separate.

species_support: human recombinant protein; mouse developmental comparator
evidence_summary: Recombinant human SCUBE2 specifically interacted with SHH and the SHH receptor PTCH1 in biochemical assays, and SCUBE2 enhanced SHH reporter activity.
limitations: The primary abstract supports biochemical interaction and enhanced reporter activity, but the accessible record does not resolve a complete ternary-complex stoichiometry or a direct SCUBE2-to-PTCH1 intracellular relay. SCUBE2 is secreted and membrane-associated, not a catalytic kinase.
consolidation_note: Batch 263 supervised SHH/SCUBE2 recovery; direct binding, extracellular release/presentation relay, and functional layers remain separate.

source_locator: PMID:22677548; PMCID:PMC3387659; DOI:10.1101/gad.191866.112; PMID:35231446; PMCID:PMC8932645; DOI:10.1016/j.devcell.2022.02.008; data/raw/evidence/module20_24_supervised_cli_phase2/retry_A20B_SHH_SCUBE2_selected_records.xml; data/raw/evidence/module20_24_supervised_cli_phase2/retry_A20B_SHH_SCUBE2_PMC3387659_fulltext.html
species_support: mouse; zebrafish developmental comparator; recombinant vertebrate protein systems
evidence_summary: SCUBE2 mediated release of dually lipidated SHH into soluble form and served as an extracellular carrier; structural work further showed GAS1-catalyzed transfer of SHH from SCUBE2 to PTCH1 during signaling-complex assembly.
limitations: The evidence establishes release and carrier/presentation functions, with GAS1 providing the catalytic handoff in the later complex-assembly study. SCUBE2, GAS1, DISP1, PTCH1, and SHH remain distinct nodes; no direct SCUBE2-to-TF interaction or universal intracellular relay is established.
consolidation_note: Batch 263 supervised SHH/SCUBE2 recovery; direct binding, extracellular release/presentation relay, and functional layers remain separate.

species_support: human tumors; mouse and cell-line metastasis models
evidence_summary: SCUBE2 facilitated release of tumor membrane-anchored SHH, activated Hedgehog signaling in mesenchymal stem cells, and promoted osteoblast differentiation; SCUBE2 neutralization or Hedgehog inhibition suppressed bone metastasis in multiple models.
limitations: This is a cancer and bone-niche model rather than a neural or SCI model. The abstract supports Hedgehog pathway activation and osteoblast differentiation but does not establish a universal terminal TF or prove that every SCUBE2 effect is mediated solely by SHH.
consolidation_note: Batch 263 supervised SHH/SCUBE2 recovery; direct binding, extracellular release/presentation relay, and functional layers remain separate.

species_support: human receptor constructs; rodent astrocyte comparator
evidence_summary: Prosaptide bound GPR37 and full-length prosaposin stimulated GPR37 signaling in receptor-expressing cells, establishing a qualified direct extracellular ligand-receptor interaction.
limitations: The study supports binding and receptor-dependent activation but uses prosaptide and full-length prosaposin in distinct assays. It does not establish a universal receptor stoichiometry or SCI-specific terminal TF.
consolidation_note: Batch 270 supervised PSAP/GPR37-family recovery; direct binding, receptor-proximal, and functional layers remain separate.

source_locator: PMID:23690594; PMCID:PMC3677493; DOI:10.1073/pnas.1219004110; PMID:24371137; PMCID:PMC3931029; DOI:10.1074/jbc.M113.510883; data/raw/evidence/module20_24_supervised_cli_phase2/retry_A20B_PSAP_GPR37_selected_records.xml
species_support: human receptor constructs; mouse/rat cellular comparators
evidence_summary: Prosaposin/prosaptide activated GPR37 through pertussis-toxin-sensitive G-protein signaling with ERK phosphorylation and inhibition of forskolin-stimulated cAMP; extracellular prosaposin also promoted GPR37 plasma-membrane association in a GM1-raft-dependent context.
limitations: Relay details are context-dependent and include both acute receptor signaling and prosaposin-dependent membrane localization. The papers do not establish a single universal downstream kinase branch across cell types.
consolidation_note: Batch 270 supervised PSAP/GPR37-family recovery; direct binding, receptor-proximal, and functional layers remain separate.

evidence_summary: Intranasal recombinant prosaposin reduced infarct volume and neuronal apoptosis and improved neurologic function after rat middle-cerebral-artery occlusion; PSAP siRNA, GPR37 siRNA, and PI3K inhibition supported a PSAP-GPR37-PI3K/Akt/ASK1 branch.
limitations: This is a rat cerebral-ischemia model, not spinal-cord injury. The study supports a pathway branch and functional protection but does not establish a direct PSAP-to-TF interaction or universal terminal TF.
consolidation_note: Batch 270 supervised PSAP/GPR37-family recovery; direct binding, receptor-proximal, and functional layers remain separate.

species_support: human receptor constructs; rodent astrocyte comparator
evidence_summary: Prosaptide bound GPR37L1 and full-length prosaposin stimulated GPR37L1 signaling in receptor-expressing cells, establishing a qualified direct extracellular ligand-receptor interaction.
limitations: The study supports binding and receptor-dependent activation but uses prosaptide and full-length prosaposin in distinct assays. It does not establish a universal receptor stoichiometry or SCI-specific terminal TF.
consolidation_note: Batch 270 supervised PSAP/GPR37-family recovery; direct binding, receptor-proximal, and functional layers remain separate.

species_support: human receptor constructs; rodent astrocyte comparator
evidence_summary: Prosaptide/prosaposin activated GPR37L1 through pertussis-toxin-sensitive G-protein signaling with ERK phosphorylation and inhibition of forskolin-stimulated cAMP in receptor-expressing cells.
limitations: The relay is defined in receptor-expressing cellular systems and does not resolve whether all endogenous GPR37L1 contexts use the same branch. GPR37L1 remains distinct from GPR37 and PTCH1.
consolidation_note: Batch 270 supervised PSAP/GPR37-family recovery; direct binding, receptor-proximal, and functional layers remain separate.

evidence_summary: GPR37L1 signaling modulated astrocyte glutamate transporters and neuronal NMDA-receptor activity, and Gpr37l1 loss increased neuronal death after MCAO; prosaptide/prosaposin-GPR37L1 astrocyte protection was also reported in the primary receptor study.
limitations: The ischemia study establishes GPR37L1-dependent neuroprotection but does not directly test full-length PSAP in every assay; the receptor paper supports prosaptide/prosaposin-dependent astrocyte protection. No universal terminal TF or SCI transfer is established.
consolidation_note: Batch 270 supervised PSAP/GPR37-family recovery; direct binding, receptor-proximal, and functional layers remain separate.

evidence_summary: Structural and NMR studies showed that the central sclerostin core, including an NXI motif, interacts with LRP5 and LRP6 β-propeller domains and that the motif is required for SOST binding to LRP5/6.
limitations: The structural and biochemical studies establish SOST binding to LRP5/6 and motif dependence, but do not establish a full-length receptor signaling conformation or a terminal TF.
consolidation_note: Batch 271 supervised SOST/LRP recovery; LRP5 layers remain separate and the LRP4 motif result is non-exportable.

evidence_summary: Sclerostin binding to LRP5/6 antagonized canonical Wnt signaling; SOST internalization and inhibition of Wnt responses were receptor- and antibody-sensitive, with context-dependent effects on Wnt1 versus Wnt3A signaling.
limitations: The relay is an extracellular receptor-antagonism mechanism with context-specific Wnt responses. LRP5 and LRP6 branches are related but not identical; no universal terminal TF is established.
consolidation_note: Batch 271 supervised SOST/LRP recovery; LRP5 layers remain separate and the LRP4 motif result is non-exportable.

evidence_summary: Sost deficiency-induced bone gain was blunted by Lrp5 loss and depended on Wnt1-class Lrp6 activity; combined Sost/Lrp5 genetics and sclerostin inhibition altered bone mass and skeletal fragility in mice.
limitations: The functional studies jointly interrogate Sost, Lrp5, and Lrp6 and therefore support a receptor-pathway output rather than an LRP5-exclusive terminal mechanism. No SCI transfer or universal terminal TF is established.
consolidation_note: Batch 271 supervised SOST/LRP recovery; LRP5 layers remain separate and the LRP4 motif result is non-exportable.

evidence_summary: In the cited structural/NMR study, the SOST loop-2 NXI motif mediated LRP5/LRP6 binding but was explicitly not involved in interaction with LRP4; this is a bounded assay result, not proof that no SOST-LRP4 interaction exists in every context.
limitations: This is a negative/boundary observation for one mapped SOST interface. It does not justify a universal no-binding claim and does not alter the frozen Module 20A LR classification.
consolidation_note: Batch 271 supervised SOST/LRP recovery; LRP5 layers remain separate and the LRP4 motif result is non-exportable.

evidence_summary: Primary cortical and hippocampal studies identify NRP2/PlexinA3 as the SEMA3F holoreceptor complex and show SEMA3F-dependent receptor-specific structural and synaptic responses.
limitations: The primary study establishes the holoreceptor components and ligand-dependent response but does not provide a purified affinity measurement for SEMA3F binding to PlexinA3 itself. NRP2 and PlexinA3 remain distinct receptor-complex nodes.
consolidation_note: Batch 273 supervised semaphorin receptor-complex recovery; supported branches and bounded exclusions remain distinct.

evidence_summary: SEMA3F-NRP2/PlexinA3 signaling required the receptor-complex cytoplasmic response for spine regulation and mediated homeostatic AMPA-receptor scaling in cortical neurons.
limitations: The relay is neuronal and developmental/homeostatic, with PlexinA3-dependent cytoplasmic signaling; it does not define a universal kinase cascade or SCI-specific mechanism.
consolidation_note: Batch 273 supervised semaphorin receptor-complex recovery; supported branches and bounded exclusions remain distinct.

evidence_summary: SEMA3F-NRP2/PlexinA3 signaling reduced dendritic spine number and excitatory synapses and mediated activity-dependent AMPA-receptor homeostatic downscaling in cortical neurons.
limitations: This is a CNS developmental/homeostatic model and does not establish an SCI outcome or universal terminal TF.
consolidation_note: Batch 273 supervised semaphorin receptor-complex recovery; supported branches and bounded exclusions remain distinct.

evidence_summary: The primary lymphatic-development study identifies NRP2 as a receptor for SEMA3G and places PlexinA2 in the SEMA3 receptor complex; receptor assignment is retained as qualified complex-level molecular evidence.
limitations: The study supports NRP2 receptor assignment and PlexinA2 complex participation in lymphatic development, but ligand-to-PlexinA2 binary binding is not isolated. SEMA3F and SEMA3G can share NRP2 but have distinct plexin contexts.
consolidation_note: Batch 273 supervised semaphorin receptor-complex recovery; supported branches and bounded exclusions remain distinct.

evidence_summary: SEMA3G-NRP2/PlexinA2-associated signaling restrained VEGFC-driven lymphatic endothelial growth and branching; genetic PlexinA2 loss increased lymphatic branching in the developmental model.
limitations: The relay is developmental and lymphatic; SEMA3G/PlexinD1 evidence is a separate complex and was not substituted for PlexinA2.
consolidation_note: Batch 273 supervised semaphorin receptor-complex recovery; supported branches and bounded exclusions remain distinct.

evidence_summary: SEMA3G and SEMA3F restrained lymphatic endothelial growth and sprouting, while Nrp2 and PlexinA2 perturbation altered dermal lymphatic branching in mice.
limitations: The Sema3G-specific PlexinA2 contribution is inferred from the combined ligand/genetic design and remains context-dependent; no universal terminal TF or SCI transfer is established.
consolidation_note: Batch 273 supervised semaphorin receptor-complex recovery; supported branches and bounded exclusions remain distinct.

evidence_summary: The primary lymphatic paper discusses SEMA3F signaling through NRP2/PlexinA3 or NRP2/PlexinA1 rather than NRP2/PlexinA2; this bounds, but does not universally exclude, the SEMA3F/PlexinA2 branch.
limitations: The paper's comparison is not a universal negative binding assay and does not alter the frozen Module 20A edge.
consolidation_note: Batch 273 supervised semaphorin receptor-complex recovery; supported branches and bounded exclusions remain distinct.

evidence_summary: The primary lymphatic study found that SEMA3G may preferentially function through PlexinA2 in lymphatic branching; it does not establish an exact SEMA3G-NRP2/PlexinA1 branch.
limitations: This is a bounded complex-context observation, not a universal no-binding claim and not a change to the frozen Module 20A edge.
consolidation_note: Batch 273 supervised semaphorin receptor-complex recovery; supported branches and bounded exclusions remain distinct.

source_locator: PMID:14657016; DOI:10.1093/emboj/cdg629; PMID:19934382; DOI:10.1369/jhc.2009.955203; PMID:25519158; DOI:10.14670/HH-30.647; data/raw/evidence/module20_24_supervised_cli_phase2/retry_A20B_PSAP_SORT1_selected_records.xml
evidence_summary: Prosaposin co-immunoprecipitated with sortilin, and C-terminal prosaposin motifs were required for sortilin binding and lysosomal targeting; the interaction is an intracellular sorting-receptor interaction.
limitations: Primary studies support a C-terminal prosaposin sorting motif and sortilin interaction, but this is mainly Golgi/lysosomal cargo trafficking rather than surface signal transduction. No universal TF or SCI transfer is established.
consolidation_note: Batch 274 supervised PSAP/SORT1 recovery; intracellular binding, trafficking relay, and phagosome/lysosome function remain distinct.

evidence_summary: Sortilin and its cytoplasmic sorting machinery routed monomeric prosaposin from the Golgi toward lysosomes, while prosaposin oligomerization separated secreted from intracellularly retained pools.
limitations: The relay concerns cargo routing and secretion/retention state, not a receptor-proximal phosphorylation cascade. Cell type and lysosomal-compartment context are essential.
consolidation_note: Batch 274 supervised PSAP/SORT1 recovery; intracellular binding, trafficking relay, and phagosome/lysosome function remain distinct.

evidence_summary: Sortilin delivered prosaposin to macrophage latex-bead phagosomes and to lysosomal compartments; Sort1 loss or dominant-negative sorting machinery impaired prosaposin delivery during phagosome maturation.
limitations: This is a macrophage and intracellular trafficking output, not a canonical ligand-induced transcriptional pathway. The result does not establish a universal sortilin-dependent function across cell types.
consolidation_note: Batch 274 supervised PSAP/SORT1 recovery; intracellular binding, trafficking relay, and phagosome/lysosome function remain distinct.

evidence_summary: TIP39/PTH2 bound PTH1R-expressing cells with weak apparent affinity of approximately 210–243 nM in radioreceptor assays, while retaining preferential activity at PTH2R.
limitations: The direct interaction is weak and pharmacologically nonproductive for full-length TIP39; the ligand identity is TIP39/PTH2 rather than canonical PTH. No SCI-specific or terminal-TF claim is established.
consolidation_note: Batch 275 supervised PTH2/TIP39-PTH1R recovery; binding, antagonist relay, and pharmacologic output remain separate.

evidence_summary: TIP39 did not stimulate cAMP at PTH1R despite binding; TIP39 and TIP39(9-39) inhibited PTH/PTHrP agonist actions, consistent with an antagonist/occupancy relay at PTH1R.
limitations: The antagonist behavior is defined in heterologous receptor and osteoblast-like cell assays and depends on peptide form. It is not a universal PTH1R physiological pathway.
consolidation_note: Batch 275 supervised PTH2/TIP39-PTH1R recovery; binding, antagonist relay, and pharmacologic output remain separate.

evidence_summary: TIP39/TIP39(9-39) inhibited PTH-, PTHrP-, and related PTH1R agonist responses in receptor-expressing cells, producing a conditional receptor-pharmacology output rather than a transcriptional endpoint.
limitations: This is receptor pharmacology and cAMP inhibition, not a defined cellular differentiation or SCI output. No universal terminal TF is assigned.
consolidation_note: Batch 275 supervised PTH2/TIP39-PTH1R recovery; binding, antagonist relay, and pharmacologic output remain separate.

evidence_summary: Co-immunoprecipitation and ligand-binding assays showed that endothelial SCUBE2 forms a complex with VEGF and VEGFR2/KDR and functions as a VEGFR2 coreceptor.
limitations: The studies support complex formation and coreceptor function but do not establish a purified binary SCUBE2-KDR affinity or a direct SCUBE2-to-TF interaction.
consolidation_note: Batch 276 supervised SCUBE2-KDR recovery; coreceptor association, VEGFR2 relay, and angiogenesis outputs remain separate.

evidence_summary: SCUBE2 enhanced VEGF-induced VEGFR2 phosphorylation and downstream AKT/MAPK signaling; SCUBE2 inhibition reduced VEGFR2 phosphorylation and proangiogenic signaling.
limitations: This is a VEGF-dependent endothelial relay with disease-context modulation. AKT/MAPK are pathway nodes, not terminal TFs, and the branch is distinct from SHH release.
consolidation_note: Batch 276 supervised SCUBE2-KDR recovery; coreceptor association, VEGFR2 relay, and angiogenesis outputs remain separate.

evidence_summary: SCUBE2 promoted VEGF-dependent endothelial growth and capillary-like network formation, was required for ischemic revascularization, and supported tumor angiogenesis; endothelial Scube2 loss or antibody inhibition reduced tumor vascularity and growth.
limitations: The outputs are vascular and tumor/ischemia-specific, not SCI-specific. The studies do not assign a universal terminal TF or prove that every SCUBE2 phenotype is exclusively VEGFR2-mediated.
consolidation_note: Batch 276 supervised SCUBE2-KDR recovery; coreceptor association, VEGFR2 relay, and angiogenesis outputs remain separate.

evidence_summary: Reciprocal BIAcore SPR assays with murine Fc-fusion proteins showed direct SECTM1A–CD7 binding, weaker/differential dissociation relative to SECTM1B, and competition for the CD7-binding context.
limitations: The same primary study identifies GITR as an alternative SECTM1A binder and shows CD7-independent T-cell co-stimulation; direct binding is therefore separate from CD7-specific relay/function attribution.
consolidation_note: Batch 277 primary full-text recovery; direct binding promoted, CD7 relay/function retained as explicit boundaries.

evidence_summary: SECTM1A functional effects on T-cell activation were reported as CD7-independent, and GITR was identified as an alternative binder; no validated CD7-specific receptor-proximal relay was established.
limitations: This is an explicit mechanistic boundary: binding is supported, but the functional receptor may be GITR or another alternative receptor. No CD7-specific kinase or TF relay is established.
consolidation_note: Batch 277 supervised SECTM1A-CD7 recovery; direct binding is separated from CD7 relay/function attribution boundaries.

evidence_summary: Immobilized or cell-surface SECTM1A enhanced IL-2 production and T-cell proliferation, but the paper reported that these outcomes were CD7-independent and therefore did not validate a SECTM1A-CD7 functional output.
limitations: The functional phenotype is real in the tested system but its receptor attribution is unresolved or CD7-independent. Terminal TF and SCI transfer remain unknown.
consolidation_note: Batch 277 supervised SECTM1A-CD7 recovery; direct binding is separated from CD7 relay/function attribution boundaries.

evidence_summary: Human resistin directly bound CAP1 in monocytes; co-immunoprecipitation, cell binding, and recombinant-protein binding assays supported the interaction.
limitations: The frozen Module 20B edge is mouse-scope, whereas this primary study uses human resistin and human CAP1. Species and ligand-isoform matching remain limiting; no direct mouse binding assay was located in this batch.
consolidation_note: Batch 278 RETN-CAP1 species matching retained; human direct/relay evidence is not silently transferred to the mouse edge.

evidence_summary: Human resistin-CAP1 signaling increased cAMP and PKA activity and was associated with NF-kB-related inflammatory transcription in human monocytes; the mouse exact-pair relay remains unresolved.
limitations: The relay is primary and exact for human resistin/CAP1, but species transfer to mouse Retn/CAP1 is not established. NF-kB-related transcription is a downstream pathway readout, not a direct TF interaction.
consolidation_note: Batch 278 RETN-CAP1 species matching retained; human direct/relay evidence is not silently transferred to the mouse edge.

evidence_summary: In BNL CL.2 mouse liver cells, recombinant mouse resistin changed insulin-resistance-related gene expression, and CAP1 siRNA altered the resistin-responsive gene program, including Jak2, Pik3r1, Socs3, Stat3, and related metabolic/inflammatory genes.
limitations: The study supports CAP1-dependent modulation of a resistin-responsive gene program, not direct mouse Retn-Cap1 binding, a purified receptor assay, TF activation, or a single linear pathway. Gene-expression changes are not equivalent to direct STAT3 or JAK2 activation.
consolidation_note: Batch 278 RETN-CAP1 species matching retained; human direct/relay evidence is not silently transferred to the mouse edge.

evidence_summary: Purified human RGMB and NEO1 ectodomains formed a direct complex with nanomolar affinity; crystal structures resolved the RGMB-NEO1 binding architecture.
limitations: The strongest direct evidence is recombinant human ectodomain structure/biophysics. The complex is a multivalent receptor-complex assembly, not evidence that NEO1 is itself a kinase or that all RGM/NEO1 outputs are identical.
consolidation_note: Batch 279 RGMB-NEO1 direct complex, receptor-complex/pathway, and mouse functional layers remain distinct; no intracellular TF interaction inferred.

evidence_summary: The primary structural study supports ligand-dependent stabilization of NEO1 dimers within supramolecular RGM-NEO1 signaling clusters; it does not identify a unique intracellular kinase relay.
limitations: The structural relay is receptor-proximal and mechanistically distinct from intracellular pathway activation. The paper expects cell- and tissue-specific downstream diversity and does not establish a universal kinase or TF.
consolidation_note: Batch 279 RGMB-NEO1 direct complex, receptor-complex/pathway, and mouse functional layers remain distinct; no intracellular TF interaction inferred.

evidence_summary: RGMB physically bridged NEO1 and GDF5 in a ternary complex; membrane-anchored RGMB inhibited GDF5 signaling in cellular assays, in contrast to RGM-mediated enhancement of selected BMP branches.
limitations: This is a ternary receptor-complex/pathway result. RGMB occupies a morphogen-receptor interface and changes GDF5 signaling; the result is not a direct molecular interaction between RGMB and an intracellular TF.
consolidation_note: Batch 279 RGMB-NEO1 direct complex, receptor-complex/pathway, and mouse functional layers remain distinct; no intracellular TF interaction inferred.

evidence_summary: In mice, Rgmb or Neo1 loss increased dividing olfactory epithelial progenitors and supernumerary sustentacular cells; both genes therefore controlled the neuron/glia production balance, while Neo1 loss also increased olfactory receptor neuron apoptosis.
limitations: The paired genetic phenotypes support pathway-level functional involvement but do not identify a unique intracellular relay, prove that every Neo1 phenotype is RGMB-dependent, or assign a terminal TF. Additional NEO1 ligands may contribute to receptor-dependent survival.
consolidation_note: Batch 279 RGMB-NEO1 direct complex, receptor-complex/pathway, and mouse functional layers remain distinct; no intracellular TF interaction inferred.

evidence_summary: PTH bound PTH1R and induced association of LRP6 with PTH1R; the primary study describes a PTH-PTH1R-LRP6 ternary complex rather than direct PTH-LRP6 binding.
limitations: The target LRP6 is a coreceptor/complex node. The paper explicitly places PTH binding on PTH1R, with LRP6 recruited into the ternary complex; direct ligand contact with LRP6 was not established.
consolidation_note: Batch 280 separates the non-direct PTH-LRP6 boundary from the PTH1R-LRP6 receptor-complex relay and mouse Sost/MEF2 functional branch.

evidence_summary: PTH-induced PTH1R-LRP6 association promoted LRP6 phosphorylation, Axin recruitment, and beta-catenin stabilization; PKA was required for the PTH-induced beta-catenin response, and LRP6 supported PTH1R G-alpha-s/cAMP signaling.
limitations: This is a receptor-complex and pathway relay downstream of PTH1R. LRP6 is not a standalone PTH ligand receptor in these assays, and the beta-catenin branch is not itself a direct TF interaction.
consolidation_note: Batch 280 separates the non-direct PTH-LRP6 boundary from the PTH1R-LRP6 receptor-complex relay and mouse Sost/MEF2 functional branch.

evidence_summary: Osteoblast/osteocyte-specific Lrp6 loss blunted intermittent-PTH suppression of Sost and altered PTH-associated MEF2C/MEF2D and HDAC responses in mouse bone, linking LRP6 to a PTH anabolic bone output.
limitations: This is a genetic/pathway attribution, not a direct molecular ligand assay. MEF2C/MEF2D are pathway-associated TF nodes in the tested bone context; universal terminal-TF assignment and SCI transfer remain unresolved.
consolidation_note: Batch 280 separates the non-direct PTH-LRP6 boundary from the PTH1R-LRP6 receptor-complex relay and mouse Sost/MEF2 functional branch.

evidence_summary: Recombinant human SLURP-1 selectively bound alpha7 nicotinic acetylcholine receptors in affinity purification and alpha7-overexpressing cells; it did not compete with alpha-bungarotoxin for the classical ligand site.
limitations: Human SLURP-1/alpha7 evidence does not establish a direct intracellular interaction or a universal downstream pathway.
consolidation_note: Batch 281 separates direct SLURP1-alpha7 binding, allosteric receptor modulation, and epithelial functional output; no intracellular TF interaction inferred.

evidence_summary: SLURP-1 caused non-competitive inhibition of acetylcholine responses through alpha7-nAChR, consistent with allosteric antagonist-like modulation outside the classical ligand site.
limitations: Receptor-proximal channel modulation is not evidence for a specific intracellular kinase or TF.
consolidation_note: Batch 281 separates direct SLURP1-alpha7 binding, allosteric receptor modulation, and epithelial functional output; no intracellular TF interaction inferred.

evidence_summary: SLURP-1 reduced keratinocyte migration and epithelialization in human cell assays and mouse wounds; its effect acted predominantly through alpha7-associated upregulation of sedentary integrins alpha2 and alpha3.
limitations: The output is receptor-associated but no unique intracellular kinase or terminal TF was established; SLURP-2 was kept separate.
consolidation_note: Batch 281 separates direct SLURP1-alpha7 binding, allosteric receptor modulation, and epithelial functional output; no intracellular TF interaction inferred.

evidence_summary: Alpha-synuclein preformed fibrils bound LAG3 with reported KD 77 nM while monomeric alpha-synuclein showed minimal binding; later structural/biophysical work attributed binding to the LAG3 D1 domain and the acidic alpha-synuclein C terminus.
limitations: The edge is species/form dependent and concerns misfolded PFFs, not an unqualified free monomer. Later work disputes the universality of neuronal LAG3 function, so direct binding and functional receptor sufficiency remain distinct.
consolidation_note: Batch 282 preserves the alpha-synuclein PFF form distinction and records conflicting LAG3 replication without averaging it into a universal receptor claim.

evidence_summary: LAG3 binding to alpha-synuclein PFFs initiated fibril endocytosis and cell-to-cell transmission in the reported models; LAG3 loss delayed PFF-induced dopamine-neuron loss and behavioral deficits.
limitations: The relay is a receptor/endocytosis and pathology-transfer mechanism, not a conventional kinase-to-TF pathway. It is challenged by later negative replication and by cell-type expression limits.
consolidation_note: Batch 282 preserves the alpha-synuclein PFF form distinction and records conflicting LAG3 replication without averaging it into a universal receptor claim.

evidence_summary: Lag3 depletion in human alpha-synuclein A53T transgenic mice reduced insoluble alpha-synuclein aggregates and glial activation, delayed disease progression, and reduced behavioral deficits.
limitations: This is a disease-model phenotype, not proof of a universal neuronal receptor mechanism. It does not identify a direct intracellular TF interaction.
consolidation_note: Batch 282 preserves the alpha-synuclein PFF form distinction and records conflicting LAG3 replication without averaging it into a universal receptor claim.

evidence_summary: A conflicting primary study found no LAG3 expression in human or murine neurons, limited specificity of alpha-synuclein fibril interaction, no worsening with LAG3 overexpression, and no effect of LAG3 depletion or knockout in tested alpha-synucleinopathy models.
limitations: This preprint directly challenges neuronal LAG3 expression and functional sufficiency. It does not erase the earlier direct PFF-binding result, but prevents universal promotion of LAG3 as the dominant neuronal SNCA receptor.
consolidation_note: Batch 282 preserves the alpha-synuclein PFF form distinction and records conflicting LAG3 replication without averaging it into a universal receptor claim.

evidence_summary: Recombinant human SLPI directly interacted with membrane phospholipid scramblase 1 in two-hybrid, pull-down, and cell-based interaction assays.
limitations: Direct evidence is human and membrane-complex focused. The paper does not establish an intracellular kinase relay or SCI-specific transfer.
consolidation_note: Batch 284 keeps PLSCR1 relay/function evidence separate from direct PLSCR4 binding and does not transfer the PLSCR1 mechanism across paralogs.

evidence_summary: SLPI binding to PLSCR1 disrupted the PLSCR1-CD4 membrane association through overlapping PLSCR1 interaction determinants, providing a membrane-complex relay relevant to HIV-1 entry.
limitations: This is a membrane-complex/entry relay rather than canonical intracellular signaling. It is specific to the tested CD4/HIV-1 context.
consolidation_note: Batch 284 keeps PLSCR1 relay/function evidence separate from direct PLSCR4 binding and does not transfer the PLSCR1 mechanism across paralogs.

evidence_summary: Physiologic recombinant SLPI inhibited HIV-1 infection of primary T lymphocytes and transfer of HIV-1 from monocyte-derived dendritic cells to autologous T cells.
limitations: The output is antiviral entry inhibition in human immune-cell models, not evidence of direct intracellular signaling or a universal SLPI function.
consolidation_note: Batch 284 keeps PLSCR1 relay/function evidence separate from direct PLSCR4 binding and does not transfer the PLSCR1 mechanism across paralogs.

evidence_summary: The primary paper reported that recombinant human SLPI interacted with phospholipid scramblase 4 and that PLSCR4 also interacted with CD4 at the T-cell surface.
limitations: The paper supports the direct interaction but does not assign a PLSCR4-specific intracellular relay or antiviral output.
consolidation_note: Batch 284 keeps PLSCR1 relay/function evidence separate from direct PLSCR4 binding and does not transfer the PLSCR1 mechanism across paralogs.

evidence_summary: No PLSCR4-specific SLPI receptor-proximal relay or PLSCR4-specific antiviral perturbation was established; the detailed CD4-disruption mechanism was mapped to PLSCR1.
limitations: This is an explicit paralog boundary within the same primary study. Direct PLSCR4 binding is retained separately, but relay and function were not resolved for PLSCR4.
consolidation_note: Batch 284 keeps PLSCR1 relay/function evidence separate from direct PLSCR4 binding and does not transfer the PLSCR1 mechanism across paralogs.

evidence_summary: Somatostatin agonist binding and receptor expression were characterized for cloned SSTR1 in Ltk- and HEK293 cells.
limitations: The assay is a cloned receptor system and does not establish a cell-specific terminal TF.
consolidation_note: Batch 285 preserves subtype-specific SSTR branches; neighboring receptor subtypes were not used as substitutes.

evidence_summary: SSTR1 mediated somatostatin inhibition of cAMP and Na+/H+ exchange; in CHO-SSTR1 cells, SSTR1 activated ERK through pertussis-toxin-sensitive G proteins, Ras, PI3K, Raf-1, and SHP-2.
limitations: The pathway is receptor-subtype matched but model dependent; ERK is a pathway node, not a direct TF interaction.
consolidation_note: Batch 285 preserves subtype-specific SSTR branches; neighboring receptor subtypes were not used as substitutes.

evidence_summary: Somatostatin activation of SSTR1 increased p21Cip1/WAF1 expression and antagonized FGF-driven proliferation in CHO-SSTR1 cells.
limitations: This is an engineered CHO-SSTR1 model and does not establish a universal SSTR1 output in SCI cells.
consolidation_note: Batch 285 preserves subtype-specific SSTR branches; neighboring receptor subtypes were not used as substitutes.

evidence_summary: Somatostatin agonist binding and cloned-receptor pharmacology were characterized for SSTR2 in Ltk- and HEK293 cells.

consolidation_note: Batch 285 preserves subtype-specific SSTR branches; neighboring receptor subtypes were not used as substitutes.

evidence_summary: SSTR2 mediated somatostatin inhibition of cAMP through a pertussis-toxin-sensitive mechanism; SSTR2 did not share the SSTR1-specific inhibition of Na+/H+ exchange.
limitations: This evidence is receptor-subtype matched but does not establish a universal downstream TF or functional output.
consolidation_note: Batch 285 preserves subtype-specific SSTR branches; neighboring receptor subtypes were not used as substitutes.

species_support: mouse; rat; human comparator studies searched

consolidation_note: Batch 285 preserves subtype-specific SSTR branches; neighboring receptor subtypes were not used as substitutes.

evidence_summary: SSTR4 was characterized by radioligand competition and agonist regulation in CHO-K1/COS-1 expression systems, with selective somatostatin analogues identified.

consolidation_note: Batch 285 preserves subtype-specific SSTR branches; neighboring receptor subtypes were not used as substitutes.

evidence_summary: SSTR4 inhibited forskolin-stimulated adenylyl cyclase and activated arachidonate release and pertussis-toxin-sensitive MAP kinase signaling in CHO-SSTR4 cells.

consolidation_note: Batch 285 preserves subtype-specific SSTR branches; neighboring receptor subtypes were not used as substitutes.

evidence_summary: SSTR5 was characterized by radioligand binding and agonist pharmacology in COS-1 expression systems, although it coupled weakly or not detectably to forskolin-stimulated cAMP inhibition in that assay.

consolidation_note: Batch 285 preserves subtype-specific SSTR branches; neighboring receptor subtypes were not used as substitutes.

evidence_summary: Somatostatin/SSTR5 activation increased MUC2 expression and secretion in mouse colon and human LS174T goblet-like cells; SSTR5 knockdown blocked the response and the pathway involved Notch-Hes1 suppression.

consolidation_note: Batch 285 preserves subtype-specific SSTR branches; neighboring receptor subtypes were not used as substitutes.

evidence_summary: HAI-1/SPINT1 extracellular protein and its Kunitz-1 domain potently inhibited matriptase/ST14 in biochemical and structure-guided studies.
limitations: The interaction is inhibitory and extracellular. No intracellular TF interaction is implied by protease inhibition.
consolidation_note: Batch 286 preserves SPINT1 inhibition of ST14/matriptase as an extracellular protease-control edge and keeps downstream HGF/MET and PAR2 outputs distinct.

evidence_summary: Induction of the matriptase/HAI-1 complex suppressed activated matriptase, reduced pro-HGF cleavage, and inhibited pro-HGF-stimulated signaling and cell scattering.
limitations: This is an extracellular protease-to-growth-factor relay. MET is a downstream receptor node and not a direct SPINT1 target in this evidence.
consolidation_note: Batch 286 preserves SPINT1 inhibition of ST14/matriptase as an extracellular protease-control edge and keeps downstream HGF/MET and PAR2 outputs distinct.

evidence_summary: HAI-1 insufficiency increased matriptase-dependent PAR2 activation in fibroblasts and promoted cancer-associated fibroblast migration; PAR2 blockade or deficiency reduced the effect.
limitations: The output is tumor/CAF-context specific and mediated through a protease-activated receptor; no direct TF interaction or universal epithelial output is established.
consolidation_note: Batch 286 preserves SPINT1 inhibition of ST14/matriptase as an extracellular protease-control edge and keeps downstream HGF/MET and PAR2 outputs distinct.

evidence_summary: Secreted F-spondin/SPON1 bound the conserved extracellular domain of APP in biochemical and cell assays.
limitations: APP is a receptor-like membrane substrate/complex node; direct binding does not imply a classical kinase relay.
consolidation_note: Batch 287 keeps SPON1-APP and SPON1-LRP8 direct, receptor-complex, and functional contexts distinct.

evidence_summary: F-spondin inhibited beta-secretase cleavage of APP, identifying a context-specific APP-processing and reduced amyloid-beta output.
limitations: The output is extracellular proteolytic processing, not a direct TF interaction or a universal neuronal outcome.
consolidation_note: Batch 287 keeps SPON1-APP and SPON1-LRP8 direct, receptor-complex, and functional contexts distinct.

evidence_summary: F-spondin interacted with ApoER2/LRP8 through its thrombospondin domain and the receptor ligand-binding domain in co-immunoprecipitation and domain-mapping assays.
limitations: The receptor is ApoER2/LRP8, distinct from APP; both can participate in a larger synaptic complex.
consolidation_note: Batch 287 keeps SPON1-APP and SPON1-LRP8 direct, receptor-complex, and functional contexts distinct.

evidence_summary: Full-length F-spondin increased APP-ApoER2/LRP8 association and surface expression; ApoER2/LRP8 clustering by F-spondin involved synaptic-complex components including APP and PSD-95.
limitations: This is a multicomponent receptor/synaptic complex, not a simple one-ligand/one-kinase pathway. APP and PSD-95 are associated nodes, not direct TF endpoints.
consolidation_note: Batch 287 keeps SPON1-APP and SPON1-LRP8 direct, receptor-complex, and functional contexts distinct.

evidence_summary: Spon1-positive inflammatory monocytes promoted LRP8-dependent TGF-beta1 activation, fibrillar collagen production, and lung-cancer metastasis; host Spon1 or tumor-cell Lrp8 loss reduced these outputs.
limitations: The output is tumor/monocyte context specific and does not establish a universal neuronal LRP8 function or direct TF interaction.
consolidation_note: Batch 287 keeps SPON1-APP and SPON1-LRP8 direct, receptor-complex, and functional contexts distinct.

evidence_summary: The primary tooth-development study supports Lrp4/Wise functional interaction and suggests extracellular-domain interaction with Wnt antagonists, but the retrieved evidence does not establish a purified direct SOSTDC1-LRP4 binding assay for this exact edge.
limitations: The evidence is strong for functional interaction but not a purified binary ligand-binding assay. This boundary does not negate context-specific physical interaction elsewhere.
consolidation_note: Batch 288 separates the direct-binding boundary from SOSTDC1-LRP4 Wnt relay and developmental function.

evidence_summary: Lrp4 mediated the Wnt-inhibitory function of Wise/Sostdc1 and modulated Wnt/beta-catenin signaling through context-dependent interactions with Wnt ligands and antagonists.
limitations: The relay is pathway/genetic and context dependent. LRP4 also has Wise-independent roles, so all LRP4 phenotypes cannot be attributed to SOSTDC1.
consolidation_note: Batch 288 separates the direct-binding boundary from SOSTDC1-LRP4 Wnt relay and developmental function.

evidence_summary: Wise/Sostdc1 and Lrp4 mutant mice showed altered Wnt/beta-catenin-dependent mammary, hair-follicle, limb, and tooth placode development; reducing Lrp5/6 or beta-catenin rescued selected Lrp4 defects.
limitations: These are developmental genetic outputs, not direct intracellular signaling measurements. LRP4 has both SOSTDC1-dependent and independent functions.
consolidation_note: Batch 288 separates the direct-binding boundary from SOSTDC1-LRP4 Wnt relay and developmental function.

species_support: human cell lines; exact species/model identity not specified in abstract
evidence_summary: TPO stimulation of c-MPL rapidly induced dose- and time-dependent tyrosine phosphorylation of JAK2 and TYK2 in two factor-dependent hematopoietic cell lines.
limitations: The abstract establishes ligand-triggered receptor signaling but not purified binary affinity, complete receptor stoichiometry, or SCI-cell transfer. Exact cell-line identity should be recovered from full text before model-specific reuse.
consolidation_note: Batch 290 preserves TPO-c-MPL relay and STAT program layers separately; no purified binding or terminal gene inferred.

species_support: human cell lines; exact species/model identity not specified in abstract
evidence_summary: TPO-c-MPL activation was associated with rapid STAT1, STAT3, and STAT5 tyrosine phosphorylation; gel-shift assays indicated STAT-containing DNA-binding complexes in myeloid factor-dependent cells.
limitations: STAT phosphorylation and gel-shift complexes are downstream pathway/program evidence, not proof of one STAT occupancy site or a terminal target gene. Exact cell-line identity and target loci remain unresolved.
consolidation_note: Batch 290 preserves TPO-c-MPL relay and STAT program layers separately; no purified binding or terminal gene inferred.

evidence_summary: In primary mouse hepatocytes, 30 microM holo-transferrin induced rapid, transient ERK1/2 phosphorylation; serum plus holo-transferrin enhanced and prolonged the response, and 10 microM U0-126 blunted the holo-transferrin-dependent hepcidin response.
limitations: The primary full text supports ligand-triggered TFR2-associated signaling in primary hepatocytes, not purified TFR2 binding affinity or a universal TFR2 kinase pathway. The article notes that TFR2 attribution is favored by transferrin subtype/context comparisons; TFR2 remains an iron-sensing/complex node.
consolidation_note: Batch 291 primary full-text recovery; transferrin receptor subtype and UTS2/UTS2B ligand-specific layers remain separate.

evidence_summary: In primary mouse hepatocytes, serum plus 30 microM holo-transferrin increased hepcidin mRNA about fourfold over serum alone; holo-transferrin also increased phospho-SMAD1/5/8, and BMP blockade with noggin or anti-BMP2/4 blunted the response. ERK inhibition reduced holo-transferrin-induced hepcidin and early phospho-SMAD1/5/8.
limitations: Hepcidin transcription is a downstream cellular output, not a direct TF-target assignment. The full text shows serum/BMP context is required, ERK contributes to the holo-transferrin response, and Smad1/5/8 phosphorylation is a pathway readout; the terminal promoter factor and direct ERK-to-Smad mechanism remain unresolved.
consolidation_note: Batch 291 primary full-text recovery; transferrin receptor subtype and UTS2/UTS2B ligand-specific layers remain separate.

evidence_summary: TFR1/TFRC mediated uptake of transferrin-bound iron in hepatocytes; hepatocyte-specific Tfr1 loss reduced transferrin iron internalization and altered systemic iron/hepcidin homeostasis.
limitations: The study supports receptor-mediated uptake and homeostasis, not a canonical intracellular signaling cascade from TFRC. TFR1 and TFR2 branches remain distinct.
consolidation_note: Batch 291 preserves transferrin receptor subtype and UTS2/UTS2B ligand-specific layers; no family or pathway substitution.

evidence_summary: Rat GPR14/UTS2R was shown to be a high-affinity receptor for UII, with dose-dependent calcium mobilization in receptor-transfected HEK293/COS-7 cells and radioligand binding to receptor membranes.
limitations: The study establishes binding/activation in recombinant systems but not endogenous SCI-cell signaling or a terminal TF.
consolidation_note: Batch 291 preserves transferrin receptor subtype and UTS2/UTS2B ligand-specific layers; no family or pathway substitution.

evidence_summary: UII stimulation of human GPR14-transfected CHO cells produced sustained ERK1/2 activation; the relay involved Gi/o coupling, PI3K, PLC, and calcium-channel mechanisms.
limitations: The relay is recombinant receptor and pharmacology dependent; no SCI receiver state or universal adaptor sequence was established.
consolidation_note: Batch 291 preserves transferrin receptor subtype and UTS2/UTS2B ligand-specific layers; no family or pathway substitution.

evidence_summary: UII increased calcium, ERK1/2 activation, c-myc induction, and DNA synthesis in porcine renal epithelial LLCPK1 cells expressing endogenous UII/GPR14; PKC and MEK inhibition reduced the growth response.

consolidation_note: Batch 291 preserves transferrin receptor subtype and UTS2/UTS2B ligand-specific layers; no family or pathway substitution.

evidence_summary: UTS2B inhibited GLP-1 secretion in mouse intestinal crypts and organoids through SSTR5 rather than its cognate UTS2R; administration to starved male mice altered GLP-1, insulin, and blood glucose.

consolidation_note: Batch 291 preserves transferrin receptor subtype and UTS2/UTS2B ligand-specific layers; no family or pathway substitution.

evidence_summary: Rat urotensin-II-related peptide/URP (UTS2B) bound and activated human or rat UTS2R/GPR14 in primary peptide/receptor studies and produced a hypotensive effect in rats.

consolidation_note: Batch 291 preserves transferrin receptor subtype and UTS2/UTS2B ligand-specific layers; no family or pathway substitution.

evidence_summary: TIMP3 was identified as an AGTR2-interacting partner by yeast-two-hybrid screening of a human ovary cDNA library.

consolidation_note: Batch 292 retains atypical receptor topology and contested APRIL-FAS attribution explicitly; no pathway-to-direct inference.

evidence_summary: Combined TIMP3 and AGTR2 treatment additively inhibited VEGF-induced HUVEC proliferation and blocked Akt and eNOS phosphorylation; AGTR2 alone also inhibited ovarian tumor growth in the experimental model.

consolidation_note: Batch 292 retains atypical receptor topology and contested APRIL-FAS attribution explicitly; no pathway-to-direct inference.
